title: Memory Management
learning_outcomes: Explain what memory management contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: references and object lifetime.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Performance work starts with a measurable target and representative workload. Profile before changing code, compare the same conditions after a change, and consider memory, cache invalidation, and regression risk. In this lesson, focus on references and object lifetime; then compare it with copy-on-write. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use memory management when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.text: Performance work starts with a measurable target and representative workload. common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
